controls.title: Access control
controls.applies_to: Any system holding company or customer data, and the accounts that reach it
controls.owner: The person accountable for security (and each system owner for their system)
controls.review_frequency: Every 100 days or sooner (quarterly); the audit flags evidence older than 100 days
controls.limitations: Showing MFA is enforced and access was reviewed does not show that a stolen session or an over-broad role would be caught
controls.objective: Every person and service has their own identity, the least access that does the job, multi-factor authentication, and a regular review.
done_when: MFA is enforced (not optional) on every human account in every system that holds company or customer data.
Production access is a separate role from non-production, and only the people who need it can assume it.
No shared accounts and no personal access tokens with broad scope in daily use.
A dated access review exists for the last quarter, with every removal acted on.

evidence_kinds.config: The access list and the MFA enforcement setting
evidence_kinds.operational: The completed access review and the offboarding record
evidence_kinds.effectiveness: A test that a removed account really cannot sign in; an attempted sign-in without MFA is refused
evidence_kinds.assurance: only where a customer, contract or plan needs it ([`../guide/paths/`](../guide/paths/))

controls.title: Secrets management
controls.applies_to: Every credential, key and token the company holds, in any environment
controls.review_frequency: Every 365 days or sooner (yearly); the audit flags evidence older than 365 days
controls.limitations: A clean secret scan and a register do not prove no secret exists somewhere unscanned, or that rotation would work in an emergency until you have done one
controls.objective: Secrets live in a secrets manager, never in code, chat or screenshots; every secret has an owner and a rotation or expiry.
done_when: A secret scan runs on every change and blocks a merge on a hit.
A register lists every secret by name, owner, last four characters and expiry; it holds no values.
Production secrets cannot be read by non-production roles.
You have rotated at least one production secret end to end, and the steps are written down.

evidence_kinds.config: The secrets register; the secret-scan configuration
evidence_kinds.effectiveness: A test that a deliberately planted dummy secret is caught by the scan; a rotation completed end to end with no outage
evidence_kinds.assurance: only where a customer, contract or plan needs it ([`../guide/paths/`](../guide/paths/))

controls.title: Change management
controls.applies_to: Every change that reaches production: code, configuration and infrastructure
controls.review_frequency: Every 100 days or sooner (quarterly); the audit flags evidence older than 100 days
controls.limitations: Branch rules show a gate exists; they do not show the whole delivery process is secure or that reviews are meaningful
controls.objective: Every change reaches production through a reviewed pull request and an automated pipeline, with a record of who approved what.
done_when: Branch rules on the production branch require a pull request and every check, with no bypass.
A sample of five recent production changes each traces to a reviewed pull request and a green pipeline run.
No shell access is used to change production code or configuration, and the host's file system is not a second copy of the code.
New pipeline checks are added to the branch rule's required list, because a check that is not listed is not enforced.

evidence_kinds.operational: Five sampled changes traced to reviews and green runs
evidence_kinds.effectiveness: An attempted merge with a red or missing check is refused
evidence_kinds.assurance: only where a customer, contract or plan needs it ([`../guide/paths/`](../guide/paths/))

controls.title: Environment separation
controls.applies_to: Development, demo and production environments and their data and credentials
controls.review_frequency: Every 365 days or sooner (yearly); the audit flags evidence older than 365 days
controls.limitations: A diagram and grants show intent; only a search and a scan show that no real data sits outside production
controls.objective: Development, demo and production are separate environments with separate data, secrets and access, and production data never flows downhill.
done_when: A written statement, enforced by access rules, that production data never leaves production.
Dev and demo contain only generated data; a spot check finds no real customer records.
The application and migration database users are separate, and the application user has no schema privileges.
The production network exposes only what is intended; a port scan confirms it.

evidence_kinds.operational: The seeder or fixture description; the external port scan
evidence_kinds.effectiveness: A check that the application's database user cannot alter the schema; a search finding no real customer data outside production
evidence_kinds.assurance: only where a customer, contract or plan needs it ([`../guide/paths/`](../guide/paths/))

controls.title: Backups and tested restores
controls.applies_to: Systems that hold business-critical data, including state outside the database
controls.owner: The owner of each system; a named restore-test owner
controls.review_frequency: Every 100 days or sooner (quarterly); the audit flags evidence older than 100 days
controls.limitations: Backup configuration shows a policy exists. A restore test shows one restoration worked. Neither proves you could recover from every plausible disaster, or meet your business's recovery needs
controls.objective: Production data is backed up automatically, encrypted, kept off the primary system, and restored on a schedule to prove it works.
done_when: Automated backups are on, encrypted, and retained for a stated period.
A restore test has been run in the last quarter, with timings and a pass or fail result.
Backups of non-database state exist and have been restored at least once.
The host's credentials can write backups but cannot read or delete them.

evidence_kinds.effectiveness: A dated restore test with timings, row counts and checksums ([`../evidence/restore-test-report.md`](../evidence/restore-test-report.md))
evidence_kinds.assurance: only where a customer, contract or plan needs it ([`../guide/paths/`](../guide/paths/))

controls.title: Logging and monitoring
controls.applies_to: Authentication, administrative and deploy events, and the alerts built on them
controls.review_frequency: Every 365 days or sooner (yearly); the audit flags evidence older than 365 days
controls.limitations: Logging being on does not show anyone reads it, or that an attack would be noticed
controls.objective: Security-relevant events are logged centrally, kept for a stated period, protected from tampering, and someone is told when something is wrong.
done_when: The cloud audit trail is on in every account and kept for the stated period.
Application, authentication and deploy logs are collected off-host.
Alerts exist for the events above and each has a named recipient.
A test alert has fired and been acknowledged.

evidence_kinds.effectiveness: A test alert that fired and was acknowledged; a sample investigation from the logs
evidence_kinds.assurance: only where a customer, contract or plan needs it ([`../guide/paths/`](../guide/paths/))

controls.title: Vendor management
controls.applies_to: Every third party that receives company or customer data, including free tools
controls.owner: Vendor owner per vendor; the privacy contact for processors
controls.review_frequency: Every 365 days or sooner (yearly); the audit flags evidence older than 365 days
controls.limitations: A register and agreements do not show a vendor is secure; a vendor's certificate is not your control
controls.objective: You know every third party that touches your data, what they hold, what contract covers it, and when you last checked them.
done_when: A vendor register exists and covers every service that receives company or customer data.
Each vendor that processes personal data has a signed data-processing agreement on file.
Critical vendors have a dated review in the last twelve months.
An exit note exists for the vendors you could not replace in a week.

evidence_kinds.effectiveness: A test of an exit path for one critical vendor (export and import)
evidence_kinds.assurance: only where a customer, contract or plan needs it ([`../guide/paths/`](../guide/paths/))

controls.title: Data protection (GDPR)
controls.applies_to: Processing of personal data that may fall within the GDPR's territorial scope (Article 3; see `scoping/gdpr-territorial-scope.md`), and anywhere else you choose to apply it
controls.owner: The accountable privacy contact (a DPO only if one is required)
controls.review_frequency: Every 365 days or sooner (yearly); the audit flags evidence older than 365 days
controls.limitations: The kit's privacy templates are a start, not legal advice or full GDPR compliance: lawful bases, rights handling and transfers need judgement and often a specialist
controls.objective: You know what personal data you hold, why, where, for how long, and how a person can see it or have it erased.
done_when: A current data inventory and record of processing exist, with a lawful basis per purpose.
Retention periods are set and a deletion has been tested.
A deletion request has been rehearsed end to end, including backups and vendors, with the time it took.
A privacy notice states the real purposes, retention and processors.
Transfers outside the EU or EEA have a recorded mechanism and assessment.
Every processor has an Art. 28 agreement.
A person is accountable for privacy, and the DPO question is answered in writing.

evidence_kinds.config: Encryption and public-access settings on stores of personal data
evidence_kinds.operational: The data inventory, record of processing, retention schedule
evidence_kinds.effectiveness: A rehearsed deletion request across systems, backups and vendors, with the time it took
evidence_kinds.assurance: only where a customer, contract or plan needs it ([`../guide/paths/`](../guide/paths/))

controls.title: Incident response
controls.applies_to: Any event that may compromise security or personal data, including near misses
controls.review_frequency: Every 365 days or sooner (yearly); the audit flags evidence older than 365 days
controls.limitations: A plan and a register show readiness and record-keeping; only a rehearsal or a real incident shows the response works
controls.objective: You have a short, rehearsed plan for detecting, containing, communicating and learning from an incident.
done_when: The plan is one page, current, and known to everyone with production access.
A tabletop exercise has been run in the last twelve months, with recorded actions.
Every incident since you started is in the register and has a written report, including near misses. If there have been none, the register says so with a start date.
Every register row involving personal data (or unknown) has a recorded notification decision with its reason.
Notification duties and contacts are listed by role, with each customer's contractual deadline kept separate from the statutory duties.

A tabletop exercise has shown that staff can tell contractual notification requirements from statutory controller deadlines ([`../runbooks/tabletop-incident-notification.md`](../runbooks/tabletop-incident-notification.md)).

evidence_kinds.effectiveness: A tabletop exercise with recorded actions that were then done
evidence_kinds.assurance: only where a customer, contract or plan needs it ([`../guide/paths/`](../guide/paths/))

controls.title: Supply chain and signing
controls.applies_to: Everything that is built and run in production, and the tools used to build it
controls.review_frequency: Every 100 days or sooner (quarterly); the audit flags evidence older than 100 days
controls.limitations: Verifying signatures shows what ran was built by your pipeline, not that the code in it is free of flaws
controls.objective: You know what is in your software, who built it, and that what runs in production is exactly what your pipeline produced.
done_when: The host verifies a signature against a pinned pipeline identity before it starts an image, and a negative test shows it refuses an unsigned one.
Vulnerability scanning blocks the build on a critical finding or records a dated exception.
Every deployed digest traces to a pipeline run and a pull request.
A software bill of materials exists for the current release.

evidence_kinds.effectiveness: An unsigned image refused by the host (the negative test)
evidence_kinds.assurance: only where a customer, contract or plan needs it ([`../guide/paths/`](../guide/paths/))

controls.title: Vulnerability management
controls.applies_to: Application dependencies, container images and operating systems, and cloud configuration
controls.review_frequency: Every 100 days or sooner (quarterly); the audit flags evidence older than 100 days
controls.limitations: Scan results show known weaknesses only; they do not find unknown flaws, and a closed ticket is not a verified fix
controls.objective: You find known weaknesses in your software and systems, rank them, fix them within stated deadlines, and record the exceptions.
done_when: Scans run automatically and their results are stored.
Severity-based deadlines are written down and applied.
Every finding past its deadline has an accepted, dated exception in the risk register.
A sample of five past findings shows detection, fix and verification dates.
A security contact for outside reports exists.

evidence_kinds.effectiveness: A verified fix: rescan shows the finding gone; the sampled past findings with dates
evidence_kinds.assurance: only where a customer, contract or plan needs it ([`../guide/paths/`](../guide/paths/))

controls.title: Risk and governance
controls.applies_to: The whole programme: roles, policies, risk decisions, training and management review
controls.owner: Founder or director responsible for security
controls.review_frequency: Every 365 days or sooner (yearly); the audit flags evidence older than 365 days
controls.limitations: Policies and a register show governance exists; they do not show people follow them or that decisions are good
controls.objective: Security is owned by named people, guided by short written policies, driven by a risk register, and reviewed by management on a schedule.
done_when: Roles and responsibilities are written down and people know theirs.
The risk register exists, is scored, and has owners and review dates.
The core policies exist, are dated, and are acknowledged by staff.
Onboarding and offboarding follow a checklist and the last leaver's record exists.
Training records exist for everyone with access.
A dated management review exists for the last twelve months, with actions.
The scoping questionnaire is current.

evidence_kinds.effectiveness: An internal review that found and fixed a gap; an independent assessment where required
evidence_kinds.assurance: only where a customer, contract or plan needs it ([`../guide/paths/`](../guide/paths/))
